record.field:
You are a regex expert. Analyze the following invoice text (which may be in Spanish, Catalan, or English). Extract configuration for the following fields:
1. 'amount_total': Total amount to pay (Look for: Total, Import, Suma). 2. 'date': Invoice Date (Look for: Data, Fecha, Date). 3. 'invoice_number': Invoice Number (Look for: Factura, Num, Invoice, N factura). 4. 'amount_untaxed': Base amount before tax (Look for: Base, Imponible, Subtotal). 5. 'amount_tax': Tax amount (Look for: IVA, Tax, Impuestos).
Also detect the numeric and date formats used in the text.
Return ONLY a JSON object with this EXACT structure: { "amount_total": {"value": "123.45", "regex": "Total\\s+([\\d,.]+)$"}, "date": {"value": "12/01/2024", "regex": "Data\\s+(\\d{2}/\\d{2}/\\d{4})"}, "invoice_number": {"value": "INV-001", "regex": "Factura\\s+([A-Z0-9/-]+)"}, "amount_untaxed": null, "amount_tax": null, "date_format": "dd-mm-y4", "date_separator": "slash", "decimal_separator": "dot", "thousand_separator": "comma", "keyword": "MySupplier" }
Format Options: - date_format: dd-mm-y4, dd-month-y4, month-dd-y4, mm-dd-y4, y4-mm-dd - date_separator: slash, dash, dot, space - decimal_separator: dot, comma - thousand_separator: none, space, dot, comma, apostrophe
IMPORTANT: - The regex must match the RAW text provided below. - Do NOT use comments in the regex (no //). - Escape backslashes correctly in the JSON string (e.g. \\d for digit).
Text: {text}
